correctness.rationale: Identity (1) exactly counts closed neighbors of each two-subset. Four inequalities (2) are necessary and sufficient for the bipartition template, including the distinct minus-one defender requirement. With a=n/2-1,b=n/2+1 and r=n/2+2-floor(b/2), H_A is a C5 for n=12 and an r-edge path for n>=14, while H_B is a maximum matching. Their degrees ensure all neighborhood sums >=1 and total weight 4. All possible smaller integer template weights are excluded by degree constraints, with the T=3 all-degree-two B case failing the internal-B inequality. Cut sizes and label-two edge sets uniquely encode the counted functions. Independent code verified direct neighborhoods for even n=12..40, symbolic identity for even n=12..128, exhaustive pattern equivalence at n=6,8 and random n=12. Finite tests do not prove all n.

value.rationale: The original Kneser paper identifies tighter signed-Roman bounds as future research. The theorem uniformly reduces the even-order gap from [2,5] to [2,4] for infinitely many graphs and gives an exact feasibility/degree characterization of the natural cut-pattern method. It also proves the four-weight threshold cannot be lowered within this method and counts a rapidly growing, explicitly reproducible family (997920 at n=12). Thus the value is not merely a finite check or a small unmotivated parameter adjustment. No global exact invariant is claimed.
